questions.answer: `os` talks to OS (getcwd, makedirs exist_ok, path.join). `pathlib` is modern object paths (`Path('r')/'2026'`, read/write_text, mkdir parents). `shutil` does bulk copy/move/rmtree. Prefer pathlib; use join// not string concat.
questions.question: Compare os vs pathlib vs shutil for Kakade's report folders.

questions.answer: strftime formats datetime->string (f=format); strptime parses string->datetime (p=parse). Use timezone-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, timedelta for arithmetic (now+timedelta(days=7)), store UTC.
questions.question: Explain strftime vs strptime and naive vs aware datetimes.

questions.answer: Counter counts + most_common; defaultdict auto-creates (int->0, list->[]) avoiding KeyError; deque fast both ends + maxlen window. re: search anywhere vs match start-only, findall all, sub replace; always raw r'...'. functools lru_cache/partial/reduce; subprocess.run list-args, capture_output/text/check, avoid shell.
questions.question: Summarize collections, re, itertools/functools, subprocess essentials.

p = Path('reports') / '2026'
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

print(Path('hello.txt').read_text())

questions.answer: match() only checks string start, so match(digits,'Kakade 123') is None — use search(). Also `(10)` is int not tuple and naive+aware datetimes can't compare; use search + (10,) + timezone.utc.

questions.answer: String concat breaks on Windows separators; use join/Path. rmtree deletes irreversibly (no trash). shell=True with user input allows injection — pass list args `['cmd','arg']` instead.
